analysis.title: Marketcolour + Earnings Snippets / ECB (Ioannis Blekos, 30 Oct 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed mixed Thursday: SPX -30bps to 7720, NDX -138bps to 28,402, RTY +101bps to 2859. 8 of 11 sectors rose. Equal-weight S&P beat cap-weight by 150bps, the third-largest single-day move YTD.

Sector dispersion was wide: Healthcare +2.50% and Real Estate +2.25%, against Communication Services -6.60%. Consumer names caught a bid on rotation out of tech, and the GS Discretionary basket (GSXUCOND) rose 3.29%.
Mega-cap tech fell on disappointing earnings. GOOG, NOW and FTNT were down 10-15% in NDX. Post-bell AMZN fell 5% and NOW fell 26.96% after a weak Q3 report.

AMZN's reported move is described as its worst single-day return in its listed history at about -12%, a 6.5-sigma move. The same note also cites AMZN at -10% (after -4% today). The two figures are not reconciled in the text.
Over 60% of SPX members are down 20% or more from their local highs. Four of the Mag7 are in bear market territory, erasing about USD 4trn of market cap.

Flow: asset managers were slight net sellers (supply in communication services and discretionary, demand in macro). Hedge fund flows were roughly flat. Single-stock activity did not rise materially despite the size of the moves, and trading felt top-down, with SPX volumes +35% vs the 20-day average.
Europe closed higher for a fourth straight day: SXXP +80bps, SX5E +60bps. Defense (GSSBDEFE +3.6%, Kongsberg +13%), software (GSSBSFTW +1.1%) and semis (GSSBSEMI +2%) outperformed.

INTC fell 17%. Q3 data center and AI (DCAI) revenue rose 78% y/y, but Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn is well below consensus of $17.29bn. Management expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through H1 of next year.
PINS fell 16%. Q3 revenue of $1.17bn missed consensus of $1.2bn, and Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance is below the Street.

SNDK was unchanged. Gross margin was 85% in the quarter, revenue beat, and EPS was nearly $50 per share. It announced an 8:1 stock split and bought back about $5bn in the quarter. Q4 revenue guidance is in line.
AMZN's AWS growth of 39% was below expectations. Management guides to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. GS reiterates Buy with a PT cut to $370 from $375, about 50% upside.

ECB: GS keeps its forecast of one more hike in December. Sovereign stress could lead to a hold, but the tightening in financial conditions required would need to be large given energy pressures. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising, but GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes.

CAP (Capgemini) beat and raised. Q3 organic growth was 5.2% vs sell-side 3.9%. Organic growth guidance was raised to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4% (Street 4.1%). Operating margin (13.6-13.8%) and organic FCF (about EUR1.8-1.9B) guidance are unchanged. Bears will focus on the book-to-bill of 89% vs a seasonal norm of 95-96%.

UMG was far better than feared. Streaming subscription growth ex-downtown was 9.5% vs Street about 8.5% and bears at 6-7%. Margin of 21.5% was 90bps ahead of the Street. GS raised FY2026+ revenue and adjusted EBITDA by about 0-1%.

Alpha Bank reported a strong beat: net profit 15% above expectations on a 6% NII beat, 2% fees beat, 3% lower expenses and lower loan loss provisions. Loans and deposits were each up 13% y/y and CET1 was 20bps better. GS expects the stock up 3-5%.
CaixaBank drew negative feedback. NII rose 5% y/y in Q3 while consensus has +13% for FY2027, so volume and NII trends may drive earnings down next year.
SCOR Q3 net income was about 17% above company-collected consensus, with a 10% beat in P&C Re and 5% in L&H Re insurance service result. GS estimates a normalised combined ratio of about 81%.

AXA Q3 gross written premiums were in line with consensus (+1%). A 3% beat in P&C and Health was offset by lower life premiums. Commercial lines P&C GWP rose 1% on a comparable basis. AXA XL price effects were -0.6% vs -2.0% in Q2, and volume was -0.4% vs the -3.0% GS assumed.
CTA positioning: GS's model has CTAs short SX5E, and they would need to buy back at current levels. The medium-term threshold is 6182 and the short-term threshold is 6238.

PINS: Q3 revenue reported at $1.17bn vs consensus estimate of $1.2bn. Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance below the Street. Stock -16%.

NOW: Fell 26.96% after a weak Q3 earnings report.

CAP: Q3 organic growth 5.2% reported vs sell-side estimate of 3.9%. Full-year organic growth guide raised to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4%, vs Street estimate of 4.1%. Operating margin guide 13.6-13.8% and organic FCF guide of EUR1.8-1.9B unchanged. Book-to-bill 89% vs seasonal norm of 95-96%.
UMG: Streaming subscription growth ex-downtown 9.5% reported vs Street estimate of about 8.5% and bears at 6-7%. Margin 21.5% reported, 90bps ahead of Street estimate.
Alpha Bank: Net profit 15% above expectations, driven by a 6% NII beat, 2% fees beat, 3% lower expenses and lower loan loss provisions. Loans and deposits +13% y/y, CET1 20bps better than expected.
CaixaBank: Q3 NII +5% y/y reported vs consensus estimate of +13% y/y for FY2027.

SCOR: Q3 2026 net income about 17% above company-collected consensus. GS estimates a normalised combined ratio of about 81%, with cats EUR12mn favourable vs budget and about EUR47mn implied buffer building.
AXA: Q3 2026 GWP in line with company-collected consensus (+1%). P&C and Health beat by 3%, offset by lower life premiums.

Sovereign stress in Europe and energy price pressure could change the ECB's path.
A continued PC slowdown through at least H1 2027 (Intel commentary).
Spanish bank NII and volume trends may weigh on 2027 earnings (CaixaBank).
